title: Virtual threads: what changes with Project Loom

videos.script: In lesson 11, ten thousand platform threads took five and a half seconds to start and a quarter of a gigabyte. This lesson starts a million. {{what}} A virtual thread is a Java thread that is not an operating system thread. A handful of carrier threads run millions of them, and a virtual thread that waits gives its carrier back to the others. {{million}} One million, started in under two seconds, with the operating system still counting twenty-seven threads. {{throughput}} Then the point of it: ten thousand tasks that each wait a tenth of a second. A pool of a hundred takes ten seconds. One virtual thread per task takes a fraction of one. {{limits}} And the limits. Virtual threads do not make computing faster, they should never be pooled, and a scarce resource still needs a limit. One limit Java 24 removed. A virtual thread waiting inside synchronized no longer holds its carrier, and the same program runs two hundred times faster on Java 25 than on 21.
